The fence appeal turns on whether the Sunset Lane ways are treated as public, which decides whether the fence bylaw applies to the abutters and could affect other homes on that street.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals moved and seconded a motion to grant a dimensional variation for a Pratt Street solar array, but the captions do not give the vote result.
The motion rests on the applicant's revised plan, with screening and fencing left to the building inspector.
The applicant's installers presented revised array dimensions and a larger setback from the northern border at the continued hearing.
The hearing went ahead with four members because one was absent, so all four had to vote in favor.
Members questioned side and rear setbacks, the rear yard and the small-scale array bylaw before the motion.

why_it_matters: A variation from setback rules on a ground-mounted solar array affects how close it sits to neighboring lots, and leaving screening to the building inspector means neighbors' protection is set outside the public hearing.
Because the vote result is not clear in the captions, whether the variance was granted has to be confirmed from the board's official decision.

meetings.headline: ZBA granted gas-station sign relief with conditions, continued a solar setback case, and extended a permit a year.

A one-year extension for a lot at 41 Country Road was also granted.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted sign relief for a new Gulf station at 400 Electric Avenue, with the pylon sign capped at the size and height of the Mobil sign on Lunenburg Shirley Road.
The same vote allowed the canopy signs as proposed, two on the front and one on the north side.
The board continued the 63 Pratt Street ground-mounted solar hearing to October 2020 (as heard), and asked for array height drawings, the leach field location and buffer options.
The board granted a one-year extension for the 41 Country Road lot and noted that a third request would be scrutinized.

why_it_matters: The sign decision sets how large and tall a new gas-station sign on Electric Avenue can be, and it ties that sign to an existing nearby one.
The solar case stays open, so the setback and buffer rules for a ground-mounted array next to neighbors on Pratt Street are not settled.
watch_next: The continued 63 Pratt Street solar hearing, set for October 2020 at 7 o'clock (as heard).
The drawings and Board of Health leach field information the applicant is to supply before that hearing.
